accepted_scope_caveats.label: prop:conditional-tie-uniform-transfer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Feasible original-experiment transfer assumes uniform two-sided total-variation experiment equivalence, legal uniformly bounded estimated games, and joint total-variation approximation; these do not follow from ordinary LAN or DQM.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The feasible regret guarantee is conditional on ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence, ass:estimated-game-legality, ass:estimated-game-kappa-bounds, and ass:joint-risk-transfer, and is secondary rather than the headline contribution.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3 gives infinitely many MMR-optimal rules under its severe-ambiguity condition, requires randomization for monotone rules based on its selected index, and excludes linear-threshold rules under differentiability; it does not characterize all arbitrary measurable one-index rules.

Theorem 1 assumes a convex centrosymmetric parameter space and derives a minimax-regret rule among all decision rules in the normal known-variance model.
The paper studies epsilon-minimax solutions when the statistician randomizes over a finite collection of I decision rules, optimizing over the (I−1)-simplex via Hedge/mirror subgradient descent.

State and prove a compact geometric lemma that an analytic sign region with one regular nonzero-curvature arc cannot equal any measurable one-index cylinder modulo Lebesgue null sets; this is the nontrivial bridge from the finite certificate to \(\mathcal D_1\)-exclusion.

Produce the rational interval-arithmetic witness or an impossibility theorem, then promote the certificate from a conditional sufficient theorem to an instantiated reproducible counter-regime against the full one-index class.
